title: Android Application Components
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of android application components using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates android application components.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Android Application Components** as part of **Kotlin for Android Development**. Android application code must respect lifecycle, UI-thread rules, accessibility, permission boundaries, and the compatibility of Android/Compose dependencies. Use the subtopics—Activities and Application Lifecycle, Intents and Navigation Concepts, Permissions and Component Communication—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Android code must account for lifecycle changes, accessibility, UI state, and platform APIs. Isolating business logic makes the interface easier to test.

items.text: Permissions and Component Communication defines a trust boundary. Validate untrusted input at the boundary, keep secrets server-side, check authorization where the protected operation occurs, and test both allowed and rejected cases.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Android Application Components removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
